analyzed_vuln.description: RWMol::replaceAtom() deletes the original Atom and updates atom bookmarks to the replacement, but does not update raw Atom pointers stored in d_stereo_groups. If the replaced atom belongs to an enhanced StereoGroup, the group retains a dangling pointer. In this PoV the stale pointer is later dereferenced by ROMol::initFromOther() at ROMol.cpp:115 while copying the recursive query molecule, causing the heap-use-after-free in Atom::getIdx(). The fix belongs in replaceAtom(): all StereoGroup references to orig_p must be redirected to atom_p (while preserving group metadata), just as bookmarks are redirected.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A crafted V2000 mol block supplies an `M  MRV SMA` recursive SMARTS. That SMARTS includes CXSMILES enhanced-stereo information so its parsed molecule has a StereoGroup referencing an atom, and a CX atom label/query form (such as one handled by processCXSmilesLabels) that causes CXSmilesOps::addquery() to call replaceAtom() on that same atom. The original atom is freed while the StereoGroup retains its address. A subsequent `M  ALS` atom-list property on the outer molecule causes ParseNewAtomList() to copy the existing RecursiveStructureQuery; RecursiveStructureQuery::copy() copies the malformed SMARTS molecule, and ROMol::initFromOther() iterates its StereoGroups and calls getIdx() on the freed atom.
